_meta.what_this_is: A 4x4 grayscale image and three 3x3 convolution kernels: a blur (weights summing to 16), a sharpen (summing to 1), and an edge detector (summing to 0). A convolution replaces each pixel with a weighted sum of its neighbors. The SUM of a kernel weights decides what it does to overall brightness: a kernel summing to 1 preserves the mean brightness, one summing to S scales it by S, and one summing to 0 produces a zero-mean result. So a blur kernel must be divided by its weight-sum (16) to keep the picture the same brightness -- forget the divide and the image gets 16x brighter.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The image and kernels are hand-authored; the kernel sums (16, 1, 0), every convolved image, and its mean brightness are computed in normalize.py. Edges use zero padding, applied identically everywhere.
